raw_response:
I will keep the plan simple and steady because my land is only 5 mu, my family also has off-farm work, and I cannot manage a very complicated system. I will split the land between maize and kidneybean instead of putting everything into one crop, because that spreads risk and also matches what I already know how to grow. I have 26 years of experience, so I will rely on familiar practices, use irrigation from the well when the crop really needs it, and avoid excessive input costs. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and give it more fertilizer because it responds well and is my main yield crop. For kidneybean, I will keep fertilizer moderate, especially nitrogen, because too much nitrogen pushes stems and leaves instead of pods. I will use rotary tillage because it is faster and fits a small farm like mine. I will spray only when needed, but I still plan for a basic number of pesticide applications because I do not want weeds, insects, or disease to reduce yield early in the season.
